RIC Orbit and Chronos: DA + ID Comparison for Cedrela

Full-horizon Central and Low comparison: physical DA baselines, restricted sequential RIC Orbit at 1h and 15 minutes, and Chronos DA + Real-Time.

Oct 21, 2026, 4:13 PM UTC

Author: Amir Torbati

Comparison boundaries and definitions

This report covers April 2028–December 2060: 393 months and 11,963Source for 11,963Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur days, including leap days, in fixed UTC+1Source for +1Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur. Calendar 2028 is a nine-month partial year. There are five cases per scenario, shown in this order: Chronos DA + Real-Time, RIC Orbit sequential DA + ID at 15 minutes and 1Source for 1Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur hour, then RIC Orbit physical DA only at 15 minutes and 1Source for 1Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur hour. All eight Orbit cases use physical 97%Source for 97%Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur availability, including the DA-only schedules saved by the outage-constrained batch. The previous joint DA + ID results are replaced in this report; the original report is preserved separately.

Site operating margin = battery market margin + direct solar revenue. Values are real-2025 euros, undiscounted, before tax, penalties, fixed OPEX, CAPEX, repowering expenditure and financing. Chronos's internal solar payment is removed from the asset split and cancels at the site boundary. This is not project free cashflow or NPV.

Financial and physical boundaries are kept separate. Chronos cash per kW grid is multiplied by 50,000Source for 50,000Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur; energy per MW grid by 50Source for 50Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur. RIC Orbit maps the 46.05 MW storage inverter through the 97.71%Source for 97.71%Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur grid efficiency to about 44.995 MW at the grid. Solar energy comparisons use grid-export-equivalent MWh. Intraday position purchases can reverse earlier DA sales without representing physical charging.

The DA-only cases here are physical Cedrela baselines with degradation and replacement. The three undegraded Ideal DA benchmarks for July 2028–June 2038 are a separate offer-assessment exercise and are not mixed into these charts.

The sequential cases compare the DA + intraday market scope in both models. Aurora labels its second market “Real-Time”; that export label is retained for traceability, not presented as an additional balancing market. Both exclude aFRR, mFRR and capacity-market income. The separate RIC Orbit DA-only baselines enable DA only.

Market participation and trading strategy are separate settings. The table lists market eligibility consistently; a separate row explains RIC Orbit's DA-first sequence and two-hour ID restrictions. Chronos's exact execution rules remain undisclosed. Each column states its own inputs explicitly.

Physical 97%Source for 97%Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur availability throughout the Orbit comparison

Every Orbit result uses the same calendar: 8,613 battery-outage hours, selected independently of prices and solar, in monthly contiguous blocks. Outages are known before optimisation; solar and the grid connection remain available. SOC carries through outages and battery charging/discharge are zero while disconnected.

The annual target remains 1.2Source for 1.2Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur cycles per calendar day, including outage days. The optimiser can compensate during available periods. RTE, capacity curves, replacement date and two-hour ID anchors are retained. The DA-only charts are the actual outage-constrained DA schedules used by the sequential cases, not the previous unrestricted-availability baselines.

Whole-site margin is close, but the asset split still matters

Read the battery and direct-solar contributions together. A higher solar contribution can offset a lower battery margin, so a similar site total is not sufficient to establish equivalent dispatch or trading realism. DA-only cases have a narrower market scope than the Chronos comparator.

DA-only, sequential DA + ID and Chronos — four annual cashflow views

Charts are grouped by metric: whole-site margin, storage purchases, storage sales and direct solar revenue. For each metric, Central and Low are shown separately, with all five cases consecutive in this order: Chronos, sequential DA + ID 15min, sequential DA + ID 1h, DA-only 15min and DA-only 1h. All bars use EUR/kW of the 50 MW grid connection; 2028 is not annualised. Negative components remain below zero.

Important change in interpretation: the sequential purchase and sales charts show settlement of signed market positions. ID purchases may buy back DA commitments, and ID sales may reduce a DA purchase. They must not be read as a physical charging/discharging breakdown. Physical energy is compared separately below. Negative prices can make a purchase a receipt or a sale a payment. Chronos's Real-Time labels and execution rules are not assumed identical.

Storage purchase cashflow — annual comparison

This is a PURCHASE-COST chart, not net intraday margin. Both DA and ID/RT purchases are plotted as negative expenditure when prices are positive; sales appear in the next section. Sequential ID buy-backs are financial position adjustments and need not represent physical charging. Net ID margin is ID sales minus ID purchases.

Separate throughput, battery margin per MWh and direct solar

The bridge decomposes the site-margin difference exactly: additional discharge valued at Chronos battery margin per MWh, the remaining battery unit-margin difference, and direct solar revenue difference. It is an accounting identity, not proof of a causal driver.

Degradation and repowering follow the inherited physical project

Sequential dispatch inherits the DA baseline's capacity, efficiency and replacement paths. It does not recalculate a new lifetime degradation path from unconstrained intraday cycling: each two-hour cycle total is held to the DA baseline, apart from documented numerical cleanup. Capacity agreement therefore reflects the input alignment and method, not an independent prediction of ageing.

RTE curves match inputs; observed output/input is a different measure

The DC–DC RTE curve is combined with inverter and grid-path efficiencies. For grid-to-grid cycling the mapped roundtrip factor includes both grid crossings and both inverter directions; solar charging follows a different path. Do not compare the DC curve directly with grid-meter output divided by charging input.

The observed ratio below is physical discharge divided by grid-meter charging plus solar charging at the AC bus. It can also reflect SOC boundary changes and energy removed by capacity adjustment. It is not a standalone measurement of the battery's DC RTE.

Similar cycle rates do not guarantee identical energy or margin

Solar allocation still differs under a sequential strategy

RIC Orbit retains solar-first charging and battery-first use of shared export headroom. Intraday can now adjust both battery and solar positions, but only inside the two-hour SOC/cycle restrictions. It is not a whole-horizon re-optimisation of the hybrid site.

These priorities can leave solar curtailed when battery discharge occupies the connection, even though a different joint site schedule might have exported more solar. The two-phase allocation and the restricted sequential adjustment can contribute to that outcome; the comparison does not isolate their causal shares.

Charging sources and dispatch patterns — 2029

The supplied Chronos exports provide monthly physical energy, not an interval dispatch schedule. We can compare charging-source totals and monthly dynamics, but cannot establish at what hour Chronos charges or discharges. The RIC Orbit hourly profiles below are averages over the full year 2029, in fixed UTC+1Source for +1Source: Validated full-horizon Cedrela sequential comparisonTables: monthly_comparison.csv, annual_comparison.csv, lifetime_comparison.csv, hour_of_day_2029.csv, runtime_and_checks.csv, VALIDATION.json, 2026-10-21_Physical_Availability_97/Outputs/<15min case>/monthly_with_transfer_accounts.csv, original monthly_comparison.csv: internal_solar_transfer_eur; Spanish summer civil time is one hour later.

Solar-first allocation may reduce purchased grid energy while maintaining discharge, but its effect on direct solar export and curtailment must also be included. The table uses comparable physical energy, not gross DA/ID traded positions.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

DA commitments now dominate the attribution; ID measures subsequent changes

DA battery and solar positions are frozen at their physical DA-baseline quantities. ID cash is the signed change from those positions multiplied by the intraday price and interval length. A purchase in ID can offset a DA sale, and a negative ID contribution can coexist with a profitable combined strategy.

This differs from assigning the whole sale to whichever simultaneous market has the higher price. Chronos's DA/Real-Time split may be consistent with sequential settlement, but the workbooks do not prove its execution sequence, foresight or price selection.

The intraday benefit is the change from the same physical DA baseline

Unlike the old joint attribution, the sequential ID cash is directly the change from frozen DA positions. Battery ID plus solar ID therefore reconciles to whole-site improvement over that same-resolution DA baseline. This is a modelled opportunity within the two-hour restrictions, not an estimate of attainable execution profit.

Completed physical-availability runs passed validation

All four sequential files and their DA baselines cover the complete requested period, including leap days. Interval cashflows reconcile to monthly totals. Validation covers SOC, energy balance, connection limits, cycle anchors and zero battery flows during outages.

The runtime table at the bottom reports the sequential ID stage, including its processing and outputs. It excludes the preceding DA solve. Saved solver minutes are summed from completed ID parts; elapsed minutes include non-solver work. These figures must not be presented as total scenario runtime. R was not rerun for this comparison.

What the comparison can and cannot establish

The report supports comparing site margin, asset split, market attribution, physical energy and lifecycle assumptions on explicit boundaries. Similar totals do not demonstrate that either model is more accurate. The sequential strategy can bring market attribution closer while its two-hour anchors also constrain potential earnings.

Chronos may differ in execution prices, liquidity, forecasting, transaction rules, availability and intraday treatment; these are not established by its monthly workbook. RIC Orbit's perfect foresight is retained but remains subject to its formulation and strategy restrictions. It is not automatically an upper bound on a differently formulated model.

The physical DA cases and the separate undegraded Ideal DA offer benchmarks answer different questions. Neither should be used interchangeably with an all-market physical revenue forecast.

Recommended next steps

  1. Review the full-horizon Central and Low site totals together with the DA/ID split and solar-energy balance.
  2. Decide whether the two-hour SOC/cycle restriction is the intended sequential strategy before making it a maintained engine option.
  3. Integrate and regression-test the numerical correction in the maintained implementation before general platform use.
  4. Keep the Ideal DA benchmark documentation and contractual denominator separate from this physical-project comparison.

Further questions

An interval Chronos dispatch export and its DA/Real-Time price/settlement definitions would enable a direct timing and execution comparison. An outage calendar would allow matched physical availability. The present results do not resolve these two gaps.

These are two accounting sensitivities on the completed physical dispatch, alongside the ten physical cases already shown. No additional solver run was required: the current solar + grid valuation option changes asset attribution without changing dispatch.

Battery margin after transfer = battery market margin − solar payment. Solar income including transfer = direct solar market revenue + solar payment. The site total is unchanged. The earlier charts deliberately retain the comparison before internal transfers; the charts here show the asset split after the selected transfer. The solar credit here is internal income, not additional direct solar exports or additional DA market sales.

The calculation follows the existing hybrid engine: solar grid-export-equivalent MWh × interval DA price. This boundary is not cell-input or AC-bus MWh. It does not assume Chronos uses that pricing rule: the Chronos lines use its actual exported solar transfer. Chronos figures here retain the report’s other exclusions, including taxes, corrective penalties and investment costs.

SOC, cycles, RTE, degradation, replacement, curtailment and all external trades are inherited unchanged. These cases do not test a different solar charging-versus-export optimisation policy.

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;

analyze_97_only.py streams all four completed physical-97% sequential dispatch files and the four matching outage-constrained DA baseline files, checks interval continuity and independently sums financial positions and physical energy. Only Chronos uses the preserved, hashed monthly extraction from the previous report; all Orbit results use physical 97% availability. Original source hashes and mappings are in Evidence/source_manifest.json.

SELECT scenario, model, SUM(site_margin_eur) AS site_margin_eur, SUM(discharge_mwh) AS discharge_mwh, SUM(cycles)/SUM(days) AS daily_cycles FROM months GROUP BY scenario, model;
